task_2.title: Restore pass-through handling for CMakeToolchain variables
task_2.description: Version 2.26.2 reverts a regression introduced in 2.26.1 where Conan automatically escaped values assigned through CMakeToolchain variables. Toolchain variable values are now emitted as provided so users retain control over raw CMake expressions and manually escaped strings.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that values assigned through `CMakeToolchain.variables` are no longer automatically escaped during CMake toolchain generation, so user-supplied strings and CMake expressions are preserved as authored.

expectation.grounded: When `CMakeToolchain` renders values from `CMakeToolchain.variables` and its configuration-specific variants, it should preserve the assigned value exactly instead of automatically escaping backslashes, dollar signs, or double quotes. This applies to ordinary toolchain variables and configuration-scoped entries, including values that intentionally contain CMake variable references such as `${...}`.
expectation.conceptual: Toolchain variables should behave as pass-through inputs. After upgrading, Conan should stop rewriting the contents of variable values and should generate CMake output that reflects exactly what the user configured.

constraints.grounded: Do not perform implicit escaping on values supplied through `CMakeToolchain.variables`. The same preservation rule must apply consistently to both global and configuration-specific variable assignments, without changing the public variable-setting API.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should restore user control over variable content without altering how users declare toolchain variables or limiting supported value forms.

behavior: Values assigned to `CMakeToolchain.variables` are emitted into generated CMake toolchain definitions without automatic character escaping.
Values assigned to configuration-specific `CMakeToolchain.variables` entries are emitted unchanged in their configuration-scoped definitions.
CMake expressions embedded in variable values, including `${...}` references, are preserved as authored rather than converted into escaped literal text.
Users are responsible for providing any escaping that their intended CMake value requires.
acceptance_criteria: When a user assigns a value containing backslashes to `CMakeToolchain.variables`, the generated toolchain should preserve the exact backslash content the user supplied and should not add extra escaping.
When a user assigns a value containing a CMake variable reference such as `${NAME}` to `CMakeToolchain.variables`, the generated toolchain should preserve that reference unchanged.
When a user assigns a configuration-specific value through `CMakeToolchain.variables`, the generated configuration-scoped toolchain definition should preserve the value exactly as authored.
When upgrading from 2.26.1 to 2.26.2, existing consumers that rely on raw or manually escaped toolchain variable values should no longer see Conan alter those values during generation.

task_1.title: Handle corrupted recipes during cache integrity checks
task_1.description: The update fixes a runtime failure in `conan cache check-integrity` when a cached recipe is corrupted. Instead of throwing an exception while building the integrity report, the command should surface the recipe as a manifest mismatch against the recipe export being checked and continue reporting integrity results.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache check-integrity` handles corrupted cached recipes by reporting them as integrity errors instead of failing with an exception.

expectation.grounded: When `conan cache check-integrity` detects that a recipe export manifest does not match the actual cached recipe contents, it should emit the normal manifest-mismatch integrity error for that recipe. The diagnostic should identify the recipe export location being checked, and the command must not raise an unrelated exception because the corrupted item is a recipe rather than a package binary.
expectation.conceptual: Cache integrity checks should gracefully detect corrupted recipes and present them as ordinary integrity failures. Users should see a clear corruption report for the affected recipe and still receive the command's normal integrity output instead of a crash.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing integrity-check outcome for valid cache entries or for package-level corruption detection. The fix is limited to recipe corruption handling and must preserve the manifest-mismatch reporting flow, including marking the affected entry as an error instead of aborting the command.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only remove the crash path for corrupted recipes without altering normal successful checks or other established corruption reports.

behavior: `conan cache check-integrity` should treat a corrupted cached recipe as a reportable integrity failure, not as an internal exception condition.
When the corrupted item is a recipe, the manifest-mismatch details should refer to the recipe/export content being validated rather than a package folder.
The integrity-check command should continue emitting results for targeted cache entries even when one of the recipes is corrupted.
acceptance_criteria: Given a cached recipe whose exported contents no longer match its manifest, when `conan cache check-integrity` runs on that entry, then it should report the recipe as an integrity error with a manifest mismatch instead of terminating with an exception.
When a manifest mismatch is reported for a corrupted recipe, the integrity output should identify the recipe/export area being checked rather than implying a package-binary location.

Given a mix of valid cache entries and a corrupted recipe, when `conan cache check-integrity` runs, then valid entries should still be reported normally and the corrupted recipe should be reported as an error in the same command output.
